(men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[Basketball Champions League]]. Smailagić was the youngest player in history to play in the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web |title=2019 NBA Draft Profile: Alen Smailagic |url=https://stats.nba.com/articles/2019-nba-draft-profile-alen-smailagic/ |website=stats.nba.com |access-date=21 June 2019 |archive-date=21 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621081807/https://stats.nba.com/articles/2019-nba-draft-profile-alen-smailagic/ |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |title=Golden State Warriors: Analyzing Alen Smailagić, the newest G-League addition |url=https://bluemanhoop.com/2018/11/01/golden-state-warriors-alen-smailagic-draft/ |website=bluemanhoop.com |date=November 2018 |access-date=19 March 2019 |archive-date=21 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190221224103/https://bluemanhoop.com/2018/11/01/golden-state-warriors-alen-smailagic-draft/ |url-status=dead }} ==Early career== Smailagić was born in [[Belgrade]], FR Yugoslavia (present-day [[Serbia]]). Smailagić started to play basketball with his hometown club [[KK Beko|Beko]]. In 2012, he joined their [[youth system]]. In the 2017–18 season, Smailagić played for Beko in the Junior Serbian League and averaged 21.7 points, 11.1 rebounds and 1.9 blocks per game over 19 games.{{cite web|title=Focus on: Alen Smailagić |url=http://www.serbiahoop.com/focus-on-alen-smailagic/|website=serbiahoop.com|date=5 February 2019 |access-date=19 March 2019}} He was named the Junior Serbian League MVP. ==Professional career== === Beko (2017–2018) === Smailagić made his senior debut for [[KK Beko|Beko]] of the semi-professional [[Serbian basketball league system|3rd-tier]] [[First Regional Basketball League (Serbia)|Serbian Regional League]] in the 2017–18 season. Over ten league games, he averaged 15.9 points, 5.0 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game. === Santa Cruz Warriors (2018–2019) === On 20 October 2018, Smailagić was selected as the 4th pick on the [[2018 NBA G League draft]] by the [[South Bay Lakers]], but he was traded right away to the [[Golden State Warriors]]-affiliated [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], which makes him the youngest player in the history of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Alen Smailagic Is The Warriors' Draft Target They Don't Want You To Know About... Yet|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jefffeld/2018/12/27/alen-smailagic-is-the-warriors-draft-target-they-dont-want-you-to-know-about-yet/#c6db0b55d858|website=forbes.com|access-date=19 March 2019}} Smailagić made his debut for the Warriors on 3 November 2018, scoring 3 points in 7 minutes he spent on the court. Over 47 league games, he averaged 9.1 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Alen Smailagic G-League Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/s/smailal01d.html |website=basketball-reference.com |access-date=21 June 2019}} === Golden State Warriors (2019–2021)=== Smailagić was drafted as the 39th pick of the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |title=2019 NBA Draft Grades: Pick-by-pick evaluations for every first- and second-round selection |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2019-nba-draft-grades-pick-by-pick-evaluations-for-every-first-and-second-round-selection/ |website=cbssports.com |date=21 June 2019 |access-date=21 June 2019}} He is the third international player drafted into the NBA from the NBA G League, joining Greek forward [[Thanasis Antetokounmpo]] and Nigerian center [[Chukwudiebere Maduabum]], and the seventh overall to play in the NBA's official minor league before being drafted by an NBA team. Smailagić was then traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in exchange for the draft rights to two future second-round picks along with cash considerations.{{cite web|title=Warriors Acquire Draft Rights to Alen Smailagić from New Orleans|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-smailagic-20190620|work=NBA.com|date=20 June 2019|access-date=23 June 2019}}{{cite web|title=Pelicans complete trade with Golden State|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-complete-trade-golden-state|work=NBA.com|date=20 June 2019|access-date=23 June 2019}} Smailagić officially signed a multi-year contract with the Warriors on 11 July 2019.{{cite web |title=Warriors Sign Jordan Poole, Eric Paschall, and Alen Smailagic |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/poole-paschall-smailagic-signings-20190711 |website=nba.com |access-date=13 July 2019}} Smailagić made his regular-season debut on 27 December 2019, recording 4 points and a rebound in a 105–96 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web |title=Alen Smailagic debuts as Warriors' furious rally gives them fourth straight win |url=http://www.knbr.com/2019/12/27/alen-smailagic-debuts-as-warriors-furious-rally-gives-them-fourth-straight-win/ |website=knbr.com |access-date=28 December 2019}} On 4 August 2021, the Warriors waived Smailagić. He appeared in 29 games (one start) over two seasons with Golden State, averaging 3.0 points and 1.5 rebounds in 7.7 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=Warriors Waive Forward Alen Smailagić|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-waive-smailagic-20210804|website=NBA.com|date=4 August 2021|access-date=4 August 2021}} === Partizan (2021–2024)=== On August 6, 2021, Smailagić officially signed a three-year deal with his hometown club [[KK Partizan|Partizan]], under head coach [[Željko Obradović]].{{cite web |title=Smailagić u Partizanu! |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2021&mm=08&dd=06&nav_id=1903284 |website=b92.net | date=8 June 2021 |access-date=6 August 2021}}{{cite web |title=Alen Smailagic moves to Partizan |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/1236010/partizan-adds-alen-smailagic/ |website=eurohoops.net |date=6 August 2021 |access-date=6 August 2021}} During the 2022–23 season, Smailagić for the first time played in [[EuroLeague]] where Partizan was eliminated from the [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in tight [[2023 EuroLeague Playoffs|playoffs]] series. Over the season, Smailagić averaged 5.4 points and 2 rebounds per game. Partizan ended the 2022–23 season by lifting the [[2022–23 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] championship trophy, after 3–2 score against Crvena zvezda in the Finals series.{{cite news |title=PARTIZAN MOZZART BET ARE 2022/23 ADMIRALBET ABA LEAGUE CHAMPIONS |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/49109/partizan-mozzart-bet-are-2022-23-admiralbet-aba-league-champions/ |access-date=23 June 2023 |work=aba-liga.com |date=22 June 2023}} Over 2023–24 season, Smailagić averaged 5.5 points and 2.2 rebounds in 31 EuroLeague games. The season was deemed to be unsuccessful for Partizan as they finished the season without lifting any trophy.{{cite news |title=Očekuje nas burno leto u Partizanu – ko ostaje, a ko odlazi? |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/srpska-kosarka/28999/ocekuje-nas-burno-leto-u-partizanu-ko-ostaje-a-ko-odlazi/vest |access-date=11 June 2024 |date=6 June 2024 |language=Serbian}} ===Žalgiris (2024–2025)=== On 28 June 2024, Smailagić signed a two-year (1+1) contract with [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Zalgiris lands explosive big man Alen Smailagic|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/zalgiris-lands-explosive-big-man-alen-smailagic/|website=EuroLeague|date=28 June 2024|access-date=30 June 2024}} ===Virtus Bologna (2025–2026)=== On 9 July 2025, Smailagić signed a two-year contract with [[Virtus Bologna]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the EuroLeague.{{cite web|title=BENVENUTO ALEN SMAILAGIC!|url=https://www.virtus.it/news/benvenuto-alen-smailagic/|website=Virtus Bologna|date=9 July 2025|access-date=9 July 2025}} ===Galatasaray (2026–present)=== On August 6, 2026, he signed a contract with the Turkish team [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.galatasaray.org/haber/basketbol/erkek-basketbol/alen-smailagic-galatasaray-mct-technicte/60714|title=Alen Smailagić Galatasaray MCT Technic'te!|last=|first=|date=August 6, 2026|website=|publisher=[[Galatasaray S.K.]]|language=Tr|access-date=August 6, 2026}} ==National team career== Smailagić was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-16 basketball team|Serbian under-16 national team]] that competed at the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] in [[Radom]], Poland. Over seven tournament games, he averaged 5.0 points, 5.7 rebounds and 0.3 assists per game.{{cite web |title=2016 Serbia 11 - Alen Smailagic |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/131821/sid/12295/tid/96799/tid2//_/2016_FIBA_U16_European_Championship/index.html
